dedupe_keys.name: regional risk and resilience sub models

description: Regional risk and resilience sub-models is a Python script collection published by the rinconraul repository and credited in its README to Rincon and Padgett. It supplies components for regional infrastructure risk assessments. The documented seismic-hazard module creates hypothetical point and line faults, samples earthquakes and generates spatially correlated ground-motion intensity measures. Users copy the scripts, create the supplied Conda environment and import functions into their own analyses; a Jupyter notebook demonstrates hazard calculations. The source is public on GitHub, free under MIT. Coverage is a user-defined regional scenario, not a published nationwide hazard inventory. Spatial detail and the simulated event sample depend on the fault geometry and analysis inputs; no fixed observation period or grid resolution is claimed. The README states two material limitations: only the AB95 ground-motion model and JB08 correlation model are implemented, and the fragility-derivation module is still under development. The collection can help construct earthquake inputs for infrastructure exposure and resilience experiments. It complements the catalogue's IN-CORE platform (platform-in-core) at the hazard-input stage, although an integration was not tested.
inputs: Hypothetical point and line fault definitions
